title: The bounded-charge global flows glue to a dense invariant direct-limit core

direct_limit_flow.core: For every finite triangular phase space X_R, define X_R^fin=union_(N<infinity) P_N X_R with the compatible Lorenz/Gauss constraints.
direct_limit_flow.density: Strong spectral convergence P_N to I in every finite Q-graph norm makes X_R^fin dense in X_R.
direct_limit_flow.global_existence: Every datum in X_R^fin lies in some bounded sector and therefore has the K1397 global large-data evolution with smooth persistence at its admitted tier.
direct_limit_flow.compatibility: K1403 and uniqueness imply S_N(t)x=S_M(t)x whenever x lies in P_M X_R and M<=N, so the sector flows glue without a choice of cutoff.
direct_limit_flow.flow_law: The glued maps S_fin(t) form a single global two-sided flow on X_R^fin and descend sectorwise through the K1400 proper classical quotient.
direct_limit_flow.conserved_data: The positive fixed-sector energy and K1404 signed spectral Noether measure are preserved on the direct-limit core.
direct_limit_flow.completion_gap: A flow on a dense union extends continuously to X_R only after a cutoff-uniform finite-time bound and Cauchy estimate. K1398 and K1406 show that neither the current base-energy restart nor a nonconstant quadratic spectral reweighting supplies that estimate.
direct_limit_flow.boundary: The theorem constructs a global dense invariant core, not a global flow on the completed unbounded-charge phase space and not a GU physical state space.
